title: How to Evaluate a Vending Machine Location
summary: A practical site-review framework covering traffic, audience, access, power, network and product demand.
intro: A good vending location is more than an empty corner. The site must support demand, safe installation and efficient replenishment.
sections: Measure daily users, peak times, dwell time and the routes people naturally take through the space.
Confirm floor area, doorway and elevator access, power, connectivity, ventilation, lighting and security.
Choose products and machine capacity around the audience, nearby alternatives and expected replenishment frequency.
content: Evaluate demand and installation constraints together before selecting a machine.

title: Cashless Payments for Unattended Retail
summary: What operators should consider when choosing card, mobile-wallet and QR payment options for vending machines.
intro: Payment hardware affects conversion, reporting and daily operations, so it should be specified early in the rollout.
sections: Choose payment methods that customers already use in the target market and location.
Confirm reliable cellular, Wi-Fi or Ethernet coverage and understand offline transaction behavior.
Align payment settlement, refunds and transaction reporting with the operator's finance workflow.
content: Treat payments as part of the operating system, not an accessory.

title: Smarter Restocking With Live Machine Data
summary: Use sales, stock and fault signals to prioritize routes and reduce unnecessary vending machine visits.
intro: The best restocking route starts with current machine data instead of a fixed calendar alone.
sections: Visit low-stock, high-selling or faulted machines first.
Turn recent sales and stock estimates into product quantities before the vehicle leaves.
Use sell-through and stockout data to refine facings, assortment and visit frequency.
content: Remote data helps operators spend time where it has the highest impact.
